uniones.resumen: Marriage, succession, purchase, renunciation and conquest brought together legally different feudos. The map must follow every effective rule, not paint all domains from the ducal inlet.
uniones.instituciones: Dijon's duchy was a French feud; the County of Burgundy, an imperial feud. Nevers and Rethel followed a smaller branch. After 1477, France took the duchy; the claims of Mary and her heirs are not equivalent to possession.

personas.resumen: The last great Valois duke of Burgundy. He died outside Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Low Countries and Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain a united state.

Heir to Charles the Bold from 1477 and titular Duchess of Burgundy. Her marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked his house to the Burgundian Netherlands. Disputes with France over the duchy, Franche-Comté and Artois mean that the entire inheritance cannot be presented as territory she governed continuously.
Habsburg emperor whose marriage policy laid the foundations of his house’s extraordinary dynastic expansion across Europe.

etapas.texto: Artois and the County of Burgundy returned to the house of Austria; Philip I and Charles V transmitted them with the Low Countries.

personas.resumen: The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Low Countries and, after Senlis in 1493, Franche-Comté and Artois. He retained the ducal title of Burgundy although the duchy was under the French crown. His marriage to Joanna I brought him to Castile and transmitted distinct inheritances to Charles V.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.

persona.resumen: Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.
Ruler of the Spanish Monarchy when its European and Atlantic power was at its height. His reign saw Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great revolt of the Low Countries.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.

Son of Stadtholder William V, he was proclaimed the first King of the Netherlands in 1815, when the kingdom also included Belgium, and became Grand Duke of Luxembourg. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 separated the south; he abdicated in 1840.

personas.resumen: Consort of the Dampierre Dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Brabant.
Victory at Worringen consolidated his control of Limburg. His career illustrates the importance of noble and urban alliances in the principalities of the Low Countries.
Duke of Luxembourg, 1353-1383. Duke of the Luxembourg dynasty.
Countess of Hainaut, 1345–1356, and a consort of the House of Avesnes.
Consort of the Burgundy dynasty. Their life was connected with Brabant.
Duke of Brabant, 1248-1261. Duke of the Brabant Dynasty.
Duke of Brabant, 1235-1248. Duke of the Brabant Dynasty.
Consort of the Hohenstaufen dynasty. Their life was connected with Brabant.

Heir to Charles the Bold from 1477 and titular Duchess of Burgundy. Her marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked his house to the Burgundian Netherlands. Disputes with France over the duchy, Franche-Comté and Artois mean that the entire inheritance cannot be presented as territory she governed continuously.
Consort of the Avesnes dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Bourbon, Hainaut.
He received the Duchy of Burgundy from his father, John II of France. His marriage to Margaret of Flanders laid the foundations for Burgundian expansion in the Low Countries.
Heiress of Flanders, Artois and the County of Burgundy, she married Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, in 1369. Her inheritance formed the foundation of her descendants’ great Burgundian state.
Duke of Burgundy and a leading figure in the French civil war. He ordered the murder of Louis of Orléans and was himself murdered at Montereau, fuelling Burgundy’s alliance with England.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was among the most brilliant in fifteenth-century Europe.

The last great Valois duke of Burgundy. He died outside Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Low Countries and Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain a united state.

The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Low Countries and, after Senlis in 1493, Franche-Comté and Artois. He retained the ducal title of Burgundy although the duchy was under the French crown. His marriage to Joanna I brought him to Castile and transmitted distinct inheritances to Charles V.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.
Noble. His trajectory is linked to Flanders.
Ruler of the Spanish Monarchy when its European and Atlantic power was at its height. His reign saw Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great revolt of the Low Countries.

Alexander Farnese was Philip II’s governor-general in the Netherlands from 1578 to 1592 and duke of Parma from 1586. The reconciliation of Artois and Hainaut and the recovery of southern towns consolidated royal authority.
Governor of the Netherlands, 1559–1567, as regent, of the Habsburg dynasty.
Governor of the Habsburg Dynasty. Their life was connected with the Low Countries.
Habsburg Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with Hungary, the Low Countries.
He ruled the Low Countries with Isabella Clara Eugenia. His regime sought to stabilize the Catholic territories and coincided with the Twelve-Year Truce.
She exercised the sovereignty over the Low Countries with Albert and then continued as governor. Her political role was much broader than that of a dynastic consort.
Count of Holland, 1304-1337. Count of the Avesnes dynasty.

personas.nombre: Ferdinand Álvarez de Toledo y Pimentel
personas.resumen: Ferdinand Alvarez de Toledo, III Duke of Alba, was Governor General of the Low Countries by Philip II between 1567 and 1573. His repressive policy and the revolt campaigns marked the government.

Son of Charles V and commander of the Holy League at Lepanto. Philip II appointed him governor-general of the Low Countries in 1576. Recognition of his authority was partial, and he eventually fought the States; he died in 1578.
Louis de Requesens and Zúñiga (1528-1576) succeeded the Duke of Alba as Governor General of the Low Countries in 1573, at the service of Philip II. He died in Brussels in March 1576.
Consort of the House of Flanders dynasty. His career is linked to France, Hainaut.

King of Spain whose government was dominated by the Duke of Lerma and an initially more peaceful foreign policy. His reign saw the expulsion of the Moriscos and the beginning of the Thirty Years’ War.

King of Spain during a period of great cultural brilliance and serious political crises. His reign, associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and the revolts in Catalonia and Portugal.
Consort of the Avesnes dynasty. Their life was connected with England and Hainaut.
Countess of Artois, 1361-1382. Countess of the Capet Dynasty.
Count of Flanders, 1322-1346. Count of the Dampierre Dynasty.
Louis of Male, Count of Flanders since 1346. In the face of the Flemish cities, his daughter Margaret took Flanders to the dukes of Burgundy.
Brabant Dynasty Consort. His trajectory is linked to Flanders, Brabant.
Brabant Dynasty Consort. His career is linked to Germany, Brabant.
Duke of Brabant, 1183-1235. Duke of the Brabant Dynasty.
Boulogne Dynasty Consort. His trajectory is linked to Brabant, Boulogne.
Brabant Dynasty Consort. His trajectory is linked to Holland, Brabant.
Count of Holland, 1222-1234. Count of the Gerulfinga dynasty.
Elected King of the Romans against the Hohenstaufen. He died on campaign against the Frisians before fully consolidating his authority.
Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and Count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland through his mother’s inheritance. His mental illness led his brother Albert to govern as regent from 1358.
Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and, through his mother Margaret, ruler of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland. He acted as regent for his brother William I and became count on William’s death in 1389.
Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland from 1404. His daughter Jacqueline inherited those counties, later contested by Philip the Good of Burgundy.
Duke of Bavaria, 1417–1425, of a Wittelsbach branch.
The last Habsburg king of Spain. His lack of descendants turned the succession into a European question and, after his death, triggered the War of the Spanish Succession.

The first Bourbon king of Spain. The War of the Spanish Succession cost him Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he briefly recovered Sardinia between 1717 and 1720. His Iberian and Italian domains followed different paths.
The Consort of the Capeto Dynasty. His career is linked to Brabant, France.
Duchess of Brabant, 1355-1406. Duchess of the Brabant dynasty.
Consort of the Valois dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Hainaut, Holland.

personas.resumen: A Habsburg emperor and Philip V’s rival in the War of the Spanish Succession. His house governed Milan, Naples and Sardinia at different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance for Maria Theresa.

Ruler of the Habsburg hereditary lands and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. She defended her inheritance in the War of the Austrian Succession and introduced important administrative reforms.

personas.resumen: A Habsburg emperor associated with enlightened absolutism. He sought a profound modernisation of the administration, Church and society of his territories through an ambitious reform programme.

personas.resumen: A Habsburg emperor whose brief reign followed his government of Tuscany. He moderated several of Joseph II’s reforms and confronted the spread of the French Revolution in Europe.

A Dutch humanist and one of the leading intellectual figures of the European Renaissance. He advocated Christian reform through education and philology without breaking with Rome.
Brother of Amadeus IV, received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders through his marriage to Joan. He was not his father's successor in Savoy County.

Prince of the house of Savoy-Carignano raised in the court of Louis XIV, passed in 1683 to the service of the Habsburg and became the great general of the Empire. He sold the Ottomans in Zenta (1697) and Belgrade (1717) and, along with Marlborough, France in Blenheim, Oudenarde and Malplatelet during the Spanish War of Succession.
Nassau Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with the Low Countries, Palatinate.
Nassau Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with the Low Countries, Brandenburg.
Governor of the Low Countries, 1751-1759 (government delegate). Orange Princess of the Hanover Dynasty.
Count of Nassau, 1416-1442. Count of the Nassau Dynasty.
Heiress of Breda from the Polanen dynasty. Her life was connected with the Low Countries.
Count of Nassau, 1442-1475. Count of the Nassau Dynasty.
Consort of the Egmond dynasty. Their life was connected with Low Countries.
Wettin Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with Saxony, the Low Countries.
The Bourbon Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with France, the Low Countries.
Coligny Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with France, the Low Countries.
Prince of Orange and the main leader of the Low Countries rebellion against Philip II. The figure was at the political origin of the future Dutch Republic.
Prince of Orange of the Nassau Dynasty. Their life was connected with the Low Countries.

Son of William of Orange, Maurice commanded the armies of the United Provinces and served as stadtholder of several provinces. His campaigns consolidated the revolt against the Spanish monarchy. He inherited the principality of Orange in 1618 and clashed politically with Johan van Oldenbarnevelt, who was executed in 1619. Maurice died in 1625.

Son of William of Orange and Louise de Coligny, Frederick Henry succeeded his half-brother Maurice in 1625 as Prince of Orange and stadtholder of several provinces. He distinguished himself in siege warfare, notably at ’s-Hertogenbosch and Maastricht. His marriage to Amalia of Solms strengthened the court and the house’s alliances.
Solms Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with the Low Countries.
Stadtholder of Low Countries, 1647–1650 (Delegated government). Prince of Orange of the Nassau dynasty.

personas.nombre: Mary, Princess Royal and Princess of Orange
personas.resumen: Orange Princess of the Estuardo Dynasty. Their life was connected with England, the Low Countries.
Daughter of James II and queen of England, Scotland and Ireland alongside William III. Her accession consolidated the dynastic and political outcome of the Glorious Revolution.
Prince of Orange and Dutch leader who became king of England alongside Mary II after the Glorious Revolution. He was one of Louis XIV’s major European opponents.
Count of Nassau, 1606-1632 (branch). Count of the Nassau Dynasty.
Stadtholder in the Netherlands, 1640–1664, exercising delegated government. A prince of the House of Nassau.
Nassau Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with the Low Countries.
Prince of Nassau, 1664–1696, of a branch of the House of Nassau.
Consort of the Ascania dynasty. Their life was connected with the Low Countries.
Prince of Nassau, 1696–1711, of a Nassau branch, and Prince of Orange.
Consort of the Hesse Dynasty. Their life was connected with Hesse, the Low Countries.
Prince of Nassau, 1711–1751, of a Nassau branch, and Prince of Orange.

personas.nombre: Wilhelmina of Prussia, Princess of Orange
personas.resumen: Princess of Orange of the Hohenzollern dynasty. Their life was connected with Prussia and Low Countries.
The last stadtholder of the United Provinces, 1751–1795. He went into exile in England in 1795 as the French arrived and the Batavian Republic was proclaimed.

Son of Stadtholder William V, he was proclaimed the first King of the Netherlands in 1815, when the kingdom also included Belgium, and became Grand Duke of Luxembourg. The Belgian Revolution of 1830 separated the south; he abdicated in 1840.
Count of Flanders, 1278–1305. Count of the Dampierre dynasty.
Consort of the Béthune Dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Flanders.
Loon- Heinsberg Dynasty Consort. Their life was connected with Nassau, the Low Countries.
Brabant Dynasty Consort. His trajectory is linked to Brabant, Savoy.
Consort of the Egmond Dynasty. Their life was connected with Guelders, Scotland.

Wife of John de Montfort and mother of the future John IV, played an active role in defending the montrfortist cause. Her performance during the Breton succession war made him a political figure with his own presence.

He inherited Flanders and Hainaut from his sister Joan. The children of their two marriages, Avesnes and Dampierre, disputed the distribution of the inheritance. The separation of both succession gave Hainaut and Flanders different family paths before their incorporation into the Burgundian group.

His marriage to Margaret of Flanders gave rise to the line of Juan de Avesnes. The dispute over the validity of that union affected the rights of their children. This family issue was part of the successive conflict between Avesnes and Dampierre.

Second husband of Margaret of Flanders and father of Guy of Dampierre. His descendants competed with that of Margaret's previous marriage for the patrimony of Flanders and Hainaut. The filiation explains why two different houses defended rights from the same mother.

He defended the rights of the Avesnes over Hainaut against his half-brothers Dampierre. The arbitration of Louis IX supported a distribution of inheritance, but did not immediately eliminate conflicts. He died before his mother; his son John II continued the comital line.

Sister of William of Holland, she married John of Avesnes. Through her, their son John II was related to the comital house of Holland. That connection proved decisive in 1299, when the death of John I of Holland allowed the inheritances of Holland and Hainaut to be united.

Count of Hainaut since 1280, inherited Holland and Zeeland in 1299 for his relationship with the Dutch house. The three counties retained their own identities. Their descendants connected them to England, the Wittelsbach and the Bourbons through marriages and successions.

He married John II of Avesnes and was the mother of William and Mary of Hainaut. His descendants linked the comital house to England, Bavaria and Bourbon. He should not be confused with his granddaughter, Philippa of Hainaut, wife of Edward III.

Succeeded Guy of Dampierre in Flanders County. His government belongs to the difficult relationship between the comital power, the Flemish cities and the French monarchy. The death of his son Louis de Nevers before he left the succession in the hands of his grandson Louis I.

The son of Robert III of Flanders and father of Louis I, died before he inherited the Flemish county. His position allows us to understand the leap between grandfather and grandson in 1322. The genealogy retains this generation even though the succession of Flanders does not include a government of its own.

He inherited Holland as a child and developed a policy that strengthened the comital power and its relations with the cities. His murder opened a stage of instability. His son John I's brief government was followed by the transmission of the inheritance to the Avesnes.

Daughter of Guy of Dampierre, married Floris V of Holland. She was the mother of John I, the last Dutch count of that male line. Her marriage linked two neighbouring houses whose inheritance would end up gathering long after under the Dukes of Burgundy.

He succeeded his father Floris V and died as a teenager without issue. John II of Avesnes derived his claim from Adelaide of Holland, his grandfather’s sister. The succession of 1299 placed Holland and Hainaut under one ruler without abolishing either county’s institutions.

He inherited Brabant as a minor, under the government of his mother Adelaide. In 1267 he gave up the duchy and the succession passed to his brother John I. His brief stage avoids turning Henry III's reversion to John I into an immediate continuity that did not occur.

Succeeded John I in Brabant and Limburg. He married Margaret of England and was the father of John III. The marriage maintained the English connection of the duchy, while the two ducal dignities continued to be transmitted under the same house.

Daughter of Edward I and Eleanor of Castile, married John II of Brabant. She was the mother of John III. Through it, the brabanzona ducal line was connected to England and Castile before its subsequent relationship with the Valois of Burgundy.

He ruled Brabant and Limburg during the first half of the 14th century. His daughters Joan and Margaret took family rights on different roads. The succession of Joan and the flamenco marriage of Margaret prepared the disputes and agreements that brought the duchy closer to the Burgundy.

personas.nombre: Marie of Évreux, Duchess of Brabant
personas.resumen: Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margaret of Artois, married John III of Brabant. She was the mother of Joanna of Brabant and Margaret, wife of Louis II of Flanders. Her descendants connect the brabanzone and Flemish successions with the Capetian branch of Évreux.
Duke of Brabant who took part in the Hundred Years’ War and died at Agincourt. His position linked the Burgundian inheritance with the Low Countries.

The first wife of Anthony de Burgundy, was the mother of John IV of Brabant and Philip of Saint- Pol. His two children successively occupied the duchies of Brabant and Limburg. The absence of descendants of both opened the inheritance to their cousin Philip the Good.

He inherited Brabant and married Jacqueline of Bavaria. The marriage drew him into the conflict over Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, but did not permanently unite those inheritances. He was succeeded by his brother Philip of Saint-Pol.

He succeeded his brother John IV in Brabant and Limburg. He died childless, and the duchies passed to Philip the Good, cousin of both brothers. This succession brought the Brabantine inheritance into the Burgundian dominions.

The son of William I of Hainaut, was also William IV of Holland. He died in a campaign in Frisia without leaving any legitimate descendants. His sister Margaret and her children placed the inheritance of the three counties in the Wittelsbach orbit.

She inherited Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland from her father and defended her rights against John of Bavaria and Philip the Good. Her marriages formed part of that political struggle. The Agreement of Delft in 1428 restricted her power, and the cession of 1433 incorporated the counties into the Burgundian inheritance.

He ruled Guelders first as a Count and then as a Duke, after the elevation of the territory in 1339. The succession faced his sons Reginald and Edward and later the descendants of his daughters. The distinction between county and duchy allows the change of rank to be maintained.

Succeeded Reginald II and lost the government to his brother Edward in 1361. He briefly returned to the duchy in 1371, after Edward's death, and died that same year. Its two stages should be set as separate mandates.

He disputed his brother Reginald III and displaced him from the government in 1361. His death in 1371 allowed a brief restoration of Reginald. The disappearance of both without descendants opened a new dispute between the lines of their sisters.

personas.nombre: Maria of Guelders, Duchess of Jülich
personas.resumen: Daughter of Reginald II, married William of Jülich and transmitted rights to his children over Guelders. Her position explains the accession of the House of Jülich after the death of his brothers. From his descendants also comes the hereditary bond of Arnold of Egmond.

He defended rights over Guelders against his sister Maria's line. The dispute pitted two female paths to the same inheritance. The victory of the supporters of Mary's son consolidated the new ducal house of Jülich.

His marriage to Mary of Guelders gave his children a position in the succession of the neighbouring duchy. The connection was not from an automatic conquest or from the name of Jülich, but from the rights of Mary. William and Reginald, both of them, ruled Guelders in turn.

He succeeded in Guelders through the rights of his mother Maria during a contested succession, securing a new territorial position for the House of Jülich. He died without legitimate descendants and was succeeded by his brother Reginald IV.

He succeeded his brother William and united Guelders and Jülich. His death without legitimate issue in 1423 once again led the two territories to different succession settlements. In Guelders, Arnold of Egmond’s claim rested on descent from a sister of Reinald.

Sister of William I and Reginald IV of Guelders, she was the mother of Mary of Arkel. Her descendants explains Arnold's claim in 1423. The succession was not a direct father-son relationship between Reginald and Arnold.

Mother of Arnold of Egmond, she transmitted the family connection to the dukes of the house of Jülich. She died before his son accessed Guelders. Her place in genealogy allows to follow hereditary rights through two generations of women.

He was elected and recognised as duke of Guelders in 1423, with rights derived from the Jülich family. His son Adolf deposed and imprisoned him; Arnold recovered power with Burgundian support. Charles the Bold’s intervention turned the family dispute into an opportunity for territorial expansion.

He married Arnold of Egmond and was the mother of Adolfo and Mary of Guelders. His family was involved in the conflict between father and son by the government of the duchy. For his mother, Catalina belonged to the family network of the Dukes of Burgundy.

He deposed his father Arnold and governed Guelders from 1465 until the Burgundian intervention of 1471. He briefly recovered the title in 1477 after Charles the Bold’s death. The Egmond dispute continued in the generation of his son Charles.

The son of Adolfo, regained the government of Guelders in 1492 and resisted the habsburgic expansion for decades. His trajectory shows that the borgognone acquisition of 1473 did not definitely close the ducal history.
Count of Nassau, 1632-1640 (branch). Count of the Nassau Dynasty.
Governor of the Low Countries, 1725-1740 (government delegate). Governor of the Habsburg Dynasty.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Philip and Margaret of Flanders
eventos.descripcion: The marriage with Margaret of Flanders prepares the union of Burgundy with rich Flemish and Borgognon territories.
John the Fearless is killed in Montereau. Philip the Good Hereda Burgundy and is approaching the English side.
Joan is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she will be executed in Rouen in 1431.
Philip the Good founded the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabel of Portugal.
Philip the Good is reunited with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Bold succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a Burgundian territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Bold
eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Mary receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.
Marriage links the Borgognon inheritance to the Habsburg and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and the County of Burgundy to the inheritance of Maria de Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther recant. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman army of Ali Bajá after hours of combat of galera against galera. The Ottoman center is falling apart, Uluç Ali is able to save part of its wing and thousands of combatants are killed, injured or held captive. The victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but it destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic victory of the coalition.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.
After the collapse of the Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings are fighting an imperial crown whose ability to impose obedience is deeply weakened.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic inheritance that extends from the Low Countries to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of the Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the continuity Habsburg
eventos.descripcion: In the course of the Austrian War of Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtained the imperial crown and showed that dignity remained elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurates the Habsburgo-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Mary Teresa and creates the Habsburgo-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, tried to reform the Habsburg domains quickly, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.

The Greek and Latin edition of Erasmus represents the humanist program of returning to the sources and subjecting the texts to a philological examination, a decisive intellectual climate for religious disputes of the 16th century.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Henry de Guise reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

In Mesina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetian, pontificas, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

Pius V accompanies the coalition with public pleas, blesses the company and sends Don Juan a pontifical banner. The Catholic memory will then associate the victory to the prayers and the Rosary; the tradition that the Pope knew the triumph before receiving the news belongs to devotional tradition, not to a fact that can be demonstrated by itself.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.

In the center, the Royal Galera of Don Juan and the Sultana of Ali Bajá are stuck in a struggle of approaches, archauces and successive reinforcements. The fall of Ali Bajá and the take of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic core of victory.

Miguel de Cervantes fights as a soldier in the Marquesa galley. He is injured during the day and loses the use of his left hand, an experience he will remember throughout his life as one of the great occasions of his time.

name: Flanders
summary: Flanders County had its own history before being integrated into the inheritance of the Dukes of Burgundy. Its cities, its textile activity and the relationship with the French crown conditioned the comital authority. The descendants of Margaret II separated the Flemish inheritance, destined for the Dampierre, from that of Hainaut, linked to the Avesnes. Later, Margaret III inherited the county of Louis of Male and her marriage to Philip the Bold connected the county with the Valois of Burgundy. The title of Countess of Margaret and her husband's government by marriage are distinguished in succession. The incorporation into Burgundy did not make the institutions of all their territories identical.

uniones.titulo: The Borgognone inheritance, feudo to feudo
uniones.resumen: Marriage, succession, purchase, renunciation and conquest brought together legally different feudos. The map must follow every effective rule, not paint all domains from the ducal inlet.

personas.resumen: The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Low Countries and, after Senlis in 1493, Franche-Comté and Artois. Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.

translatedSource.resumen: Flanders County had its own history before being integrated into the inheritance of the Dukes of Burgundy. Its cities, its textile activity and the relationship with the French crown conditioned the comital authority. The descendants of Margaret II separated the Flemish inheritance, destined for the Dampierre, from that of Hainaut, linked to the Avesnes. Later, Margaret III inherited the county of Louis of Male and her marriage to Philip the Bold connected the county with the Valois of Burgundy. The title of Countess of Margaret and her husband's government by marriage are distinguished in succession. The incorporation into Burgundy did not make the institutions of all their territories identical.

eventos.descripcion: The marriage with Margaret of Flanders prepares the union of Burgundy with rich Flemish and Borgognon territories.
John the Fearless is killed in Montereau. Philip the Good Hereda Burgundy and is approaching the English side.
Joan is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she will be executed in Rouen in 1431.
Philip the Good founded the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabel of Portugal.
Philip the Good is reunited with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Bold succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a Burgundian territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Mary receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.

The agreement returns Artois and the County of Burgundy to the inheritance of Maria de Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther recant. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic inheritance that extends from the Low Countries to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of the Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the continuity Habsburg
eventos.descripcion: In the course of the Austrian War of Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtained the imperial crown and showed that dignity remained elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurates the Habsburgo-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Mary Teresa and creates the Habsburgo-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, tried to reform the Habsburg domains quickly, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Henry de Guise reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

summary: The medieval county of Holland is not equal to all the Netherlands. His comital house was linked to Flanders, Brabant and the Avesnes. The death of John I without descendants in 1299 brought the inheritance to John II of Avesnes, already Count of Hainaut. The post-Wittelsbach transmission was marked by the struggle between Margaret and her son William, and the separation between the ownership of William and the government of his brother Albert. Much later, the break-up with Philip II again altered the relationship between the claimed title and recognized authority.

The great visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

name: Moldova
summary: The continuity of the Moldovan princes was conditioned by restorations, external interventions and conflicts of the boyars. The links of Petru Rareș connect their descendants with Serbia and Wallachia. Elena Branković, Chiajna and Ruxandra played different roles: being a consort, running a government and transmitting kinship are not interchangeable categories.

eventos.titulo: Rodolfo of Habsburg is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The election of Rodolfo I closes the Great Interregno and places the Habsburgs for the first time at the centre of imperial politics.

eventos.titulo: Marchfeld and the Austrian Habsburg base
eventos.descripcion: The defeat and death of Otakar II allows the consolidation of the habsburgic appropriation of Austria and Styria, the territorial base of a dynasty that will still take generations to monopolize the imperial crown.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of the Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the continuity Habsburg
eventos.descripcion: In the course of the Austrian War of Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtained the imperial crown and showed that dignity remained elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurates the Habsburgo-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Mary Teresa and creates the Habsburgo-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, tried to reform the Habsburg domains quickly, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.

eventos.titulo: The Battle and Relief of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens up a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the Leopold I monarchy is mixed with the imperial rivalry in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski are putting together mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

eventos.titulo: Polish, imperial and German princes meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces while contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories join him of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes over the command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgs, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war that began in 1683 is becoming a Habsburg expansion by Hungary and is a lasting alteration to the balance of Central Europe.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman army of Ali Bajá after hours of combat of galera against galera. The Ottoman center is falling apart, Uluç Ali is able to save part of its wing and thousands of combatants are killed, injured or held captive. The victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but it destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic victory of the coalition.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

In Mesina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetian, pontificas, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

Pius V accompanies the coalition with public pleas, blesses the company and sends Don Juan a pontifical banner. The Catholic memory will then associate the victory to the prayers and the Rosary; the tradition that the Pope knew the triumph before receiving the news belongs to devotional tradition, not to a fact that can be demonstrated by itself.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.

In the center, the Royal Galera of Don Juan and the Sultana of Ali Bajá are stuck in a struggle of approaches, archauces and successive reinforcements. The fall of Ali Bajá and the take of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic core of victory.

name: Montferrat
summary: The Imperial March of the Aleramici, in the 14th century, passed to a branch of the Palaiologoi for the rights of Irene, daughter of William VII and Byzantine empress. The links with Majorca, Savoy and Saluzzo added rights and rivalries. The legacy of Margaret Paleologue then linked the marquisate to the Gonzaga, maintaining a different institutional trajectory from Mantua.

One of the main allergenic marquis, he extended his influence through cities in northern Italy. His daughter Yolanda married Andronikos II and took the name Irene.
Born Yolanda, a daughter of William VII, she adopted the name Irene when she married Andronikos II Palaiologos. The marriage connected Montferrat with the Byzantine imperial court.

A son of Andronikos II and Irene of Montferrat, he moved from the Byzantine imperial family to the rule of an Italian marquisate. His rights came through his mother, but he had to defend them against rival claimants.

The son of John James, he succeeded his brother William VIII when expectations about the inheritance of Montferrat already affected Savoy and Saluzzo. His sons William IX and John George extended the male line of Palaiologoi.

He inherited Montferrat from Boniface III and married Anne of Alençon. His children Margaret and Boniface would occupy different positions in the succession: Boniface inherited the marquisate, while Margaret transmitted the rights that would eventually support its incorporation into the Gonzaga inheritance.

The wife of William IX, she served as guardian for their son Boniface IV and defended Palaiologan interests during the Italian Wars. She also took part in the marriage negotiations that united her daughter Margaret with Frederick II Gonzaga.
The son of William IX and Anne of Alençon, he inherited Montferrat at the age of six, under guardianship. He died young and without descendants, so he was succeeded by his uncle Juan Jorge.
A son of Boniface III and brother of William IX, he succeeded his nephew Boniface IV. He was the last marquis of the legitimate male Palaiologos line.

eventos.titulo: The symbolic beginning of the Lutheran Reform
eventos.descripcion: The dispute over indulgences makes Martin Luther the center of a dispute that soon overcomes academic debate and questions authority, doctrine and obedience.
Charles V demands that Luther recant. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic inheritance that extends from the Low Countries to Spain and America.
The confrontation with Johann Eck pushes Luther beyond the question of indulgences: the discussion reaches the papal authority, the reconciliations and the primacy of Scripture.
Reformist princes and cities protest against the reversal of religious concessions. The name that will end up identifying the Protestant churches is born from this political protest.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.

eventos.titulo: The Battle and Relief of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens up a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Augusto the Strong gets the crown
eventos.descripcion: The election of Saxony becomes Catholicism and is able to be elected king. Poland - Lithuania is personally united with Saxony and its choice makes the crown a European issue.
Estanislao Leszczyński and Augusto III are proclaimed by rival factions. The dispute leads to a European war and shows how far the neighbouring powers can condition electoral freedom.

eventos.titulo: The May 3 Constitution tries to change the system
eventos.descripcion: The new constitution eliminates the liberum veto and replaces the elective monarchy with an hereditary succession envisaged in the house of Saxony. It is the most ambitious attempt to reform the Republic from within.

eventos.titulo: Polish, imperial and German princes meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces while contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories join him of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes over the command of the relief operation.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.

The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.

eventos.titulo: The Battle and Relief of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens up a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the Leopold I monarchy is mixed with the imperial rivalry in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski are putting together mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

eventos.titulo: Polish, imperial and German princes meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces while contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories join him of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes over the command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgs, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war that began in 1683 is becoming a Habsburg expansion by Hungary and is a lasting alteration to the balance of Central Europe.

The Ottoman center is falling apart, Uluç Ali is able to save part of its wing and thousands of combatants are killed, injured or held captive. The victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but it destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic victory of the coalition.

In Mesina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetian, pontificas, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.
